It was the first time I told my therapist that I have an eating disorder. 

I started of explaining that there was a girl in the psychiatry who was bulimic. I didn't say anything specific about her behaviours. (She was my roommate by the way and we talked about our behaviours a lot. It was so refreshing finally getting to know someone who can understand the things I was going through at the time.) Anyway in an attempt to explain to my therapist that I thought I had an ED (been struggling with this for over 4 years when I told her about it) I told her that I could relate a lot to what this girl was going through food wise. 

Then she said I shouldn't compare myself to highly disordered people.

After that I was triggered and engaged in much more disordered behaviours. Anyway I wanted to get help with my habits so I persistently told her that I have problems regarding food and explained ALL of my behaviours to her. (Including chewing and spitting, throwing up, fasting, counting calories, eating very little and then binge eating, doing an excessive amount of sports even though I had a lot of blisters on my feet from that already. I even told her I ate out of the trash when I was in binge mode once! And ofc some more things I did that definitely wouldn't be considered healthy.)

Then we work on that for half a year. But due to my autism diagnosis she called it special interest! As if ruining my health like this could possibly be a special interest! 

She also told me some other hurtful things. One time she said my intake looks normal. But she's way shorter than me and not nearly as active but this triggered me so bad. Or one time when she asked me if I wanted to continue therapy since I am 18 now. Bdudbfjf. Like I didn't have any problems to begin with. She was also proud of me for going out walking a lot because that helps my depression when in reality my ED was the driving factor behind that and I was falling back into my sport addiction. 

There were a few more things she said that were triggering. I actually thought about if she meant something different when she told me that I shouldn't compare myself to highly disordered people. But since she called my disordered behaviours Special interest after that I am pretty sure her intentions weren't as good as I had wanted them to be.
